records.claim_scope: In the ideal diffusion model, $I=I_S\left(e^{qV/(k_BT)}-1\right)$: current $I$, reverse saturation current $I_S$, junction voltage $V$, elementary charge $q$, absolute temperature $T$ and Boltzmann constant $k_B$. See del Alamo, MIT 6.012, [lecture 14](https://web.mit.edu/6.012/www/SP07-L14.pdf) (2007), pp. 13–16. This is a model with a range of validity, not an exact law for every diode; recombination, series resistance, high injection and breakdown require further treatment. The tenfold increase per roughly 60 mV is the forward-current approximation at 300 K with ideality factor one; the depleted layer in the figure uses the approximation that mobile charge there is negligible.

records.claim_scope: P. A. M. Dirac, [‘A Theory of Electrons and Protons’](https://doi.org/10.1098/rspa.1930.0013), *Proceedings of the Royal Society A* 126 (1930): 360–365, and [‘Quantised Singularities in the Electromagnetic Field’](https://doi.org/10.1098/rspa.1931.0130), 133 (1931): 60–72. The latter replaces the proton identification with an anti-electron. A semiconductor hole is an effective excitation, not a positron; ‘cancel’ means recombination, not literal matter–antimatter annihilation. Efficient LEDs generally use direct-gap materials, unlike silicon. For silicon’s 1.12 eV gap and intrinsic carrier density near $10^{10}$ cm$^{-3}$ at 300 K, see C. A. Ross, MIT 3.15, [‘Carrier Fundamentals’](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/3-15-electrical-optical-magnetic-materials-and-devices-fall-2006/a3b94baf512eac5e3272b6f2f9b59467_lecture1.pdf), pp. 1–2. More fully, $n_i=\sqrt{N_cN_v}\,e^{-E_g/(2k_BT)}$, where $N_c,N_v$ are effective densities of states; the omitted prefactor itself varies with temperature. The exponential alone is not the fraction of atoms supplying carriers.

records.claim_scope: W. Kohn and J. M. Luttinger, [‘Theory of Donor States in Silicon’](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.98.915), *Physical Review* 98 (1955): 915–922. The hydrogen picture uses screened interaction and effective mass, not changed fundamental constants. An isotropic estimate with relative permittivity about 11.7 and mass about $0.26m_e$ gives a radius near 2.4 nm and binding near 0.026 eV; valley anisotropy and the donor’s immediate surroundings matter for the actual ground state. Phosphorus’s measured binding is about 0.045 eV; see Ross, [‘Carrier Fundamentals’](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/3-15-electrical-optical-magnetic-materials-and-devices-fall-2006/a3b94baf512eac5e3272b6f2f9b59467_lecture1.pdf), p. 1. At room temperature, dilute donors can be largely ionized even though this exceeds $k_BT$; state populations, not a hard energy cutoff, determine ionization. One-part-per-million doping gives about $5 \times 10^{16}$ donors per cm$^3$. For the purity scale, Tokuyama specifies [eleven-nines polysilicon](https://www.tokuyama.co.jp/eng/products/electronic_materials/polysilicon.html/); purity specifications depend on the impurities counted.
